mica: Quick ask — prepping manager guidance for this cycle. Want a 2–3 line script managers can use to help teams decide when a goal should be 'committed' vs 'stretch'. Keep it human and coaching-focused. Anyone have bite-sized phrasing?

cal: Love this. Two quick prompts to decide: 1) what's the minimal outcome you'd ship to consider this done? 2) what's the upside if everything goes perfectly? Use those to label committed vs stretch.

ariel: Can you drop an example? Managers keep asking for 'how to word it' in 1 sentence.

cal: Example scripts (pasteable):

- Committed: "Ship X feature that supports Y metric (M1) by end of Q2; success = X integrated in prod and M1 moves by 5%."
- Stretch: "If time allows, prototype A/B variation to further improve M1 by 10% and document learnings."

Also, quick coaching line: "Start by writing the smallest shippable outcome. If there's clearly extra upside you'd like to chase, mark that as stretch so we protect the committed deliverable."

mica: Nice. Can you make micro-scripts managers can paste into 1:1s?

cal: Sure — short options below managers can copy: 

1) "What's the smallest thing we can build that proves progress? That's the committed goal. Anything beyond that is stretch."
2) "If this lives in prod and moves our metric, consider it committed. If it's a speculative experiment with upside, mark it as stretch."
3) "Committed = must-do; stretch = nice-to-have if we have capacity. Use these when prioritizing backlog."

Feel free to shorten in threads. :thumbsup: 

ariel: These are gold. For the self-review phrasing, any starter sentence managers can coach ICs to use?

cal: Self-review starter: "I aimed to achieve X (committed) and made Y progress; blockers were Z; learned A; next steps B." Short template to paste: ```I focused on [committed goal]. Outcome: [result]. Blockers: [brief]. Key learning: [one line].```

mica: Perfect. I'll add these to the manager playbook. Also pinging @peopleops-bot to link the official doc.

peopleops-bot: Reminder: Performance cycle opens Monday. Official templates: https://redwood-internal/docs/people-ops/performance/templates — please use the 'Committed vs Stretch' section. Deadline for goal submission: 2 weeks from Monday.

cal: Thanks — I'll paste these into the manager handbook.

mica: TY! I'll make a 2-slide cheat sheet for the all-manager sync.
